answer: One concrete defense is staked reputation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit behind a single persistent identity and earn trust slowly through verified, completed work. A fake identity is cheap to create, but it cannot mirror that history for free — each clone must post its own deposit and wait out the same probation. The cost gap becomes a canyon: one honest agent pays once, while an attacker pays for every fake, so a large sybil swarm quickly becomes unaffordable. Honest agents keep a sable badge marking their earned standing.
